section: 6.4 Human-Centered and Socio-Technical Evaluation Gaps
text: Current evaluation frameworks for watermarking and fingerprinting remain critically under-specified along three interlocking human-centered dimensions: perceptual fidelity as experienced by diverse readers, linguistic equity across sociotechnically marginalized language communities, and the systemic collateral harms arising from misuse or misinterpretation of provenance signals.

section: 6.4 Human-Centered and Socio-Technical Evaluation Gaps

section: 6.4 Human-Centered and Socio-Technical Evaluation Gaps
text: To close these gaps, we advocate a tripartite augmentation of evaluation practice: (1) participatory assessment protocols embedding GPT-4-Judge–guided instruction-following evaluation with structured human fluency/accuracy ratings across age, education, and linguistic background; (2) cross-lingual fairness auditing that treats RTT not as an attack but as a *baseline requirement*, mandating layered embedding-time/post-generation signals validated on low-resource language benchmarks; and (3) misuse impact modeling that formalizes false attribution as a constrained optimization problem—e.g., minimizing the KL divergence between watermark detection logits and ground-truth authorship labels under adversarial prompt distributions—thereby transforming ethical redlines into verifiable statistical constraints.
